title: Lifecycle Stage Vocabulary
purpose: Defines the canonical lifecycle stage identifiers used by workflows, execution reports, provenance records, and orchestration components to refer to bounded-initialization stages with stable machine-readable names.

stages.purpose: Validate and normalize the JSON initialization request and extract all authority-bearing fields.
Resolve the exact local source revision and inventory its material for selection.
Preflight the destination and filesystem to verify the destination is absent or empty and supports same-filesystem atomic promotion.
Establish the staging transaction by creating an isolated same-filesystem staging workspace at the destination.
Select and install reusable repository framework material from the source revision into the staging workspace.
Generate product foundations from the explicit product identifier and supplied direction material.
Assemble the immutable origin provenance record and write it into the staged repository content.
Assemble handoff inputs and write the handoff manifest into the staged repository content.
Establish the deterministic local Git repository including all final staged artifacts.
Validate repository content and Git state against conformance requirements.
Finalize the external execution result by recording the workflow outcome and preparing the caller return value.
Atomically promote the complete staged directory to the declared destination.
Execute a hosting-platform profile against the promoted repository as a post-promotion stage.

normative_requirements.text: Every stage identifier defined in the lifecycle stage vocabulary shall be unique, shall use lowercase-kebab-case format, and shall be stable across specification versions.

Workflows, execution reports, provenance records, and orchestration components that reference bounded-initialization stages shall use the canonical stage identifiers defined by this vocabulary and shall not introduce ad-hoc stage names.
Each stage definition shall declare its purpose, whether it is required or optional, whether it may be deferred, whether failure is recoverable, its predecessor stage identifiers, and its output.

A stage declared as required must execute in every workflow that includes its stage identifier; a stage declared as optional may be skipped when the execution profile or workflow definition explicitly omits it.

A stage declared as non-recoverable (such as promotion) shall not be retried after failure without an explicit recovery or cleanup workflow; a recoverable stage may be retried after its predecessor conditions are re-established.
Predecessor stage identifiers declared for a stage shall refer only to other stages defined in this vocabulary, and the predecessor relation shall not form a cycle.
